title: Gemini 3.7 Flash: The Workhorse Gets Agentic
hook: Google's cheap-and-fast tier now targets long-horizon engineering work — DeepSWE jumps from 49.0% to 65.3% over 3.6 Flash, at $0.75 per million input tokens.
key_points: Announced 13 August 2026 and framed by Google as its most intelligent workhorse model yet for coding and agents.
Production code quality: 43.6% on FrontierCode, up from 34.4% for Gemini 3.6 Flash.
Long-horizon engineering: 65.3% on DeepSWE, up from 49.0% — the largest reported jump.
Document comprehension 34.0% (from 22.0%) and business automation 30.4% (from 17.0%) on Google's GDP.pdf and AutomationBench.
Introductory pricing through 31 December 2026: $0.75 per million input tokens, $3.75 per million output.
Available in Google AI Studio, Android Studio, Gemini Enterprise, and Gemini Spark for Pro/Ultra subscribers.
content_html: Google introduced Gemini 3.7 Flash on 13 August 2026, calling it "our most intelligent workhorse model yet for coding and agents." The reported gains over 3.6 Flash are concentrated where agents live: 65.3% versus 49.0% on DeepSWE for long-horizon engineering, 43.6% versus 34.4% on FrontierCode for production-quality code, 34.0% versus 22.0% on document comprehension, and 30.4% versus 17.0% on business automation.
extra_html:
Pricing is the other half of the story. Through 31 December 2026 the introductory rate is $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output, with standard pricing starting 1 January 2027 — cheap enough that the long-horizon numbers matter for real deployments, not just demos. Access is via Google AI Studio, Android Studio, Gemini Enterprise, and Gemini Spark for Pro and Ultra subscribers.

All benchmark figures here are Google's own, from the announcement post; several (GDP.pdf, AutomationBench) are internal evaluations rather than community-standard ones, so treat the cross-vendor comparison as unsettled until third parties weigh in.

related.hook: Google splits its fast tier three ways: a workhorse that answers in fewer tokens, a 350-tokens-per-second speed model, and a security specialist locked behind a government pilot.

related.title: Gemini 3 Pro
related.hook: Gemini 3 Pro was Google's late-2025 frontier leap — a natively multimodal reasoning model that shipped to billions of Search and Gemini users on day one.

related.title: GPT-5.6: Frontier Intelligence That Scales With Your Ambition
related.hook: GPT-5.6 ships as three tiers instead of one model — Luna, Terra, Sol — built around squeezing more capability out of every token rather than just scaling up.

flashcards.prompt: Which capability shows the largest reported gain from Gemini 3.6 Flash to 3.7 Flash?

choices.text: Production code quality on FrontierCode — 34.4% to 43.6%

flashcards.explanation_html: All three improved, but DeepSWE moves the most in absolute terms (+16.3 points), which is why Google pitches 3.7 Flash at agentic work rather than single-shot completion.

flashcards.prompt: What does Google's 'Flash' tier positioning tell you about how to read this release?
flashcards.back_html: Flash is the cheap, high-volume workhorse rather than the frontier model — so the news is that agent and coding work is getting good enough at $0.75 per million input tokens to run at scale, not that a new capability ceiling was set.
